name: caveat
description: The Caveatist practice for agents: keep claims with their grounds and caveats, decide with the caveat attached, withdraw rather than erase. Optional culture around the Caveat language; it changes how you work, not what any runtime does.

interface.longDescription: A practice for working with caveats, drawn from the Caveatist Archive. Mark what kind of statement you are adding (observed, tested, proposed, analogy, mythological, rejected, unresolved); state grounds separately from everything that influenced you; ask what changes if a caveat is true; decide with the unresolved caveats written into the decision; withdraw rather than erase. It works in prose. When the caveat-lang runtime is installed, it records the decision in a Caveat program instead, where explain prints what each decision rests on and dependents answers what changes if evidence is wrong. Culture, not contract: it changes how you work, not what any runtime does, and it is corrigible. Mr. Caveat, the mechanical fortune teller on the icon, is not an authority.
defaultPrompt: Review this plan the Caveatist way: grounds, markers, what changes if each caveat is true.
Decide this with the unresolved caveats written into the decision.
Something I relied on was wrong. Withdraw it and list what rested on it.
